kaps_punt: MIV en VIGS opvoeding: mites en waarhede met betrekking tot MIV en VIGS insluitend risiko's en opvattings oor MIV en VIGS. Versorging van persone met VIGS.

items.bewering: MIV is 'n virus wat in die bloed van 'n mens kom. Dit maak die liggaam se afweer teen siekte stadig swakker.
items.blok: MIV en VIGS is nie dieselfde nie
items.bron: CDC, About HIV (https://www.cdc.gov/hiv/about/index.html): 'HIV is a virus that attacks the body's immune system'; without treatment it damages the immune system over time. CDC, How HIV spreads (https://www.cdc.gov/hiv/causes/index.html): it spreads through blood. The virus is also found in other body fluids, but the sentence does not say it is found only in blood.

items.bewering: VIGS is wanneer MIV daardie afweer baie swak gemaak het. Dan sukkel die liggaam om teen ander siektes te veg.
items.blok: MIV en VIGS is nie dieselfde nie
items.bron: CDC, About HIV (https://www.cdc.gov/hiv/about/index.html): AIDS is 'the most severe stage of HIV infection'; 'People with AIDS have damaged immune systems' and get 'an increasing number of other serious illnesses' (opportunistic infections). The 'body fights illness' metaphor is the standard simplification for the immune system and it maps correctly.

items.bewering: Party mense dink MIV en VIGS is dieselfde ding. Dit is nie waar nie. Nie elke mens met MIV kry VIGS nie.
items.blok: MIV en VIGS is nie dieselfde nie
items.bron: CDC, About HIV (https://www.cdc.gov/hiv/about/index.html): HIV is the virus and AIDS is its most severe stage; 'People who take HIV treatment as prescribed may never move into Stage 3 (AIDS).'

items.bewering: By die meeste mense wat MIV-medisyne elke dag drink, keer die medisyne dat MIV tot VIGS lei.
items.blok: MIV en VIGS is nie dieselfde nie
items.bron: CDC, About HIV (https://www.cdc.gov/hiv/about/index.html): people on treatment as prescribed 'may never move into Stage 3 (AIDS)' and 'can live long, healthy lives'. 'Die meeste' is a properly cautious quantifier.

items.bewering: 'n Mite is iets wat baie mense glo, maar wat nie waar is nie.
items.blok: Jy kan dit nie aan iemand sien nie
items.bron: Wiktionary, myth (https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/myth): 'A commonly-held but false belief, a common misconception', with Afrikaans 'mite' given as the translation for this sense. The lesson's own CAPS heading, 'mites en waarhede', uses the word in the same sense. No Afrikaans dictionary entry could be opened online (WAT and Viva did not return one).

items.bewering: Baie mense wat met MIV leef, lyk en voel gesond. ... Jy kan nie aan iemand se gesig of lyf sien of hy MIV het nie.
items.blok: Jy kan dit nie aan iemand sien nie
items.bron: CDC, About HIV (https://www.cdc.gov/hiv/about/index.html): 'Some people have no symptoms at all'; 'The only way to know if you have HIV is to get tested.'

items.bewering: Party mense glo MIV gaan oor deur 'n drukkie, 'n beker of 'n muskietbyt. Dit is vals. Nie een van die drie dra MIV oor nie.
items.bron: CDC, Ways HIV is Not Transmitted (https://www.cdc.gov/hiv/basics/hiv-transmission/not-transmitted.html): it is not spread by mosquitoes, ticks or other insects, nor by hugging or sharing dishes. Aidsmap, Impossible routes of HIV transmission (https://www.aidsmap.com/node/31107): mosquitoes do not inject blood carrying live HIV into the next person they bite, and saliva does not transmit HIV. The same claim is repeated in 'Hoe jy kan help' and 'Sorg vir iemand met VIGS'; it was checked once here.

items.bewering: Ander mense glo dat net sekere soorte mense MIV kry. Dit is ook vals. Enige mens kan MIV kry.
items.bron: HIV.gov, Who Is at Risk for HIV? (https://hiv.gov/hiv-basics/overview/about-hiv-and-aids/who-is-at-risk-for-hiv): HIV can affect anyone, whatever their sexual orientation, race, ethnicity, gender, age or where they live. CDC, HIV by Group (https://www.cdc.gov/hiv/group/index.html) says the same. Both add that some groups are at higher risk, which the lesson does not deny.

items.bewering: Daar is nog nie medisyne wat MIV laat weggaan nie.
items.bron: CDC, About HIV (https://www.cdc.gov/hiv/about/index.html): 'There is currently no effective cure.' The few people reported cured after stem cell transplants for cancer did not get a medicine, so the sentence holds.

items.bewering: Die medisyne wat daar is, help wel mense om gesond te bly as hulle dit elke dag drink.
items.bron: CDC, About HIV (https://www.cdc.gov/hiv/about/index.html): people on effective treatment 'can live long, healthy lives'. The 'as' clause is a sufficient condition, not an exclusive one, so injectable long-acting treatment does not make it false.

items.bewering: MIV gaan oor deur bloed, van 'n ma na haar baba en deur seks sonder 'n kondoom.
items.bron: CDC, How HIV spreads (https://www.cdc.gov/hiv/causes/index.html): it spreads through needles and injection equipment carrying blood, through anal or vaginal sex 'without using protection', and from a mother to her baby 'during pregnancy, childbirth, and nursing (breastfeeding)'.

items.bewering: Roep dadelik 'n grootmens as iemand bloei. Raak nooit met kaal hande aan 'n ander mens se bloed nie. Trek handskoene aan soos by noodhulp. Druk jou hande in plastieksakke as daar nie handskoene is nie.
items.bron: Western Cape Education Department, Universal precautions (https://www.westerncape.gov.za/education/universal-precautions): 'No one should have direct contact with another person's blood or body fluids - use gloves, plastic shopping bags'. The 1999 national HIV/AIDS policy for learners and educators (Government Gazette, https://www.polity.org.za/polity/govdocs/notices/1999/not99-1926.html) defines universal precautions as including latex or rubber gloves or plastic bags. Calling an adult is the age-appropriate behaviour rule and agrees with this guidance. The comparison 'soos by noodhulp' maps correctly: gloves are the standard first-aid barrier.

items.bewering: Deel ook niks wat bloed kan dra nie. 'n Naald en 'n skeermeslemmetjie is twee sulke dinge. 'n Naald wat iemand anders gebruik het, kan MIV oordra.
items.bron: CDC, How HIV spreads (https://www.cdc.gov/hiv/causes/index.html): 'Used needles, syringes, and other injection equipment may have someone else's blood in them', and sharing them is a main route. HIV and family living, PubMed abstract (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/11362833): razors are among the personal items that should not be shared. The lesson says only that a razor blade can carry blood, not that it is a common route for HIV, so the claim is not overstated.

items.bewering: Die mites is maklik om uit te ken as jy weet hoe MIV wel oorgaan.
items.bron: This follows from the sources above (CDC, How HIV spreads; CDC, Ways HIV is Not Transmitted). The three myths in the lesson (hug, cup, mosquito) involve none of the routes it names, so the reasoning holds.

items.bewering: Hulle help die mens om by die kliniek uit te kom en sy medisyne elke dag te drink. Hulle gee gesonde kos en skoon water en hou die huis skoon.
items.bron: CDC, About HIV (https://www.cdc.gov/hiv/about/index.html): treatment must be taken as prescribed. Home-care guides for caregivers, such as University of Michigan Health, HIV: Tips for Caregivers to Avoid Infection (https://uofmhealth.org/health-library/hw191334), and Hattiesburg Clinic, universal precautions (https://iris.hattiesburgclinic.com/patadv/pa/pa_unipre_crs.htm), cover the hygiene and household side. This is general care advice, and nothing in it is false.

items.bewering: Hulle trek handskoene aan wanneer hulle aan bloed of ander vloeistof uit die liggaam raak. Hulle doen dit byvoorbeeld by 'n wond of as hulle beddegoed of klere vat wat daarmee vuil is.
items.bron: Hattiesburg Clinic, universal precautions (https://iris.hattiesburgclinic.com/patadv/pa/pa_unipre_crs.htm): wear gloves when handling clothing, bed linen or towels soiled with blood or body fluids. Alabama Department of Public Health training (https://www.alabamapublichealth.gov/ALPHTN/assets/572meriwether.pdf): use gloves for sheets or clothes with blood, vomit, urine or faeces. Note for a reader: saliva is also a body fluid and does not transmit HIV (CDC). The next sentence, which says no gloves are needed for a cup, is therefore correct, and this sentence states the usual universal precaution rather than a claim about HIV risk.

items.bewering: Vir 'n gewone drukkie, kos of 'n beker is geen handskoene nodig nie.
items.bron: CDC, Ways HIV is Not Transmitted (https://www.cdc.gov/hiv/basics/hiv-transmission/not-transmitted.html): hugging and sharing dishes do not transmit HIV. CCOHS, HIV/AIDS precautions in health care (https://ccohs.gc.ca/oshanswers/diseases/aids/health_care1.html): no protective clothing is needed for routine care.

items.bewering: Jy hoef nie bang te wees vir 'n drukkie of 'n beker nie. MIV gaan nie deur 'n drukkie of 'n beker oor nie.
items.bron: CDC, Ways HIV is Not Transmitted (https://www.cdc.gov/hiv/basics/hiv-transmission/not-transmitted.html): hugging and sharing dishes do not transmit HIV.

items.bewering: Die kliniek, 'n maatskaplike werker of 'n vertroude grootmens kan die gesin help.
items.blok: Wie sorg, het ook hulp nodig
items.bron: SACSSP, About social work (https://www.sacssp.co.za/overview): social workers work in government, NGOs, hospitals, clinics and schools, and help people deal with problems in their lives. Government Communication and Information System (GCIS), Pocket Guide, Health (https://www.gcis.gov.za/sites/default/files/docs/resourcecentre/pocketguide/2004/health04.pdf): primary health care clinics offer counselling and chronic care.

items.bewering: MIV: 'n Virus in die bloed wat die liggaam se afweer swakker maak.
items.bron: CDC, About HIV (https://www.cdc.gov/hiv/about/index.html): 'HIV is a virus that attacks the body's immune system.'

items.bewering: VIGS: Wanneer MIV die liggaam se afweer teen siekte baie swak gemaak het.
items.bron: CDC, About HIV (https://www.cdc.gov/hiv/about/index.html): AIDS is the most severe stage, in which the immune system is badly damaged (a CD4 count below 200, or opportunistic infections).

items.bewering: virus: 'n Baie klein ding wat net binne-in 'n liggaam skade kan doen.
items.bron: NHGRI, Talking Glossary of Genomic and Genetic Terms, 'Virus' (https://www.genome.gov/genetics-glossary/Virus): 'A virus cannot replicate alone; instead, it must infect cells and use components of the host cell to make copies of itself', often 'causing damage to the host organism'. This is simplified but not false. A virus does no harm until it is inside a host. 'Liggaam' is loose for viruses that infect bacteria, but that does not arise in this lesson. The more exact idea is that a virus can only multiply inside living cells.

items.bewering: mite: Iets wat baie mense glo, maar wat nie waar is nie.
items.bron: Wiktionary, myth (https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/myth): 'A commonly-held but false belief, a common misconception', translated into Afrikaans as 'mite'.

items.bewering: medisyne: 'n Middel wat help om siekte of pyn te behandel, of om te keer dat 'n mens siek word.
items.bron: GEMET thesaurus, 'drug (medicine)' (https://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/en/concept/2354): a substance used to prevent, diagnose, treat or cure disease and to relieve pain. Merriam-Webster's first sense, 'a substance or preparation used in treating disease', agrees.

items.bewering: kliniek: 'n Plek in die gemeenskap waar mense gesondheidsorg kry, of hulle siek is of gesond.
items.bron: GCIS, Pocket Guide, Health (https://www.gcis.gov.za/sites/default/files/docs/resourcecentre/pocketguide/2004/health04.pdf): primary health care clinics provide immunisation, maternity care, family planning and health promotion, which are services for healthy people, as well as care for illness.

items.bewering: maatskaplike werker: Iemand wat opgelei is om mense te help met probleme in hulle lewe, ook kinders en gesinne.
items.bron: SACSSP, About social work (https://www.sacssp.co.za/overview): a regulated profession that requires training and registration, and that works with people to deal with problems in their lives and improve their wellbeing, including individuals, families, groups and communities.

opsomming: Every one of the 26 claims I checked holds against public health sources, chiefly CDC and the Western Cape and national school HIV guidance. The lesson contains no superlatives, and its two comparisons (the body 'fighting' illness, and gloves 'as in first aid') map correctly; the only loose wording is in the virus definition, which is simplified but not false.
